occasions.moment: the 4pm dip at a desk — hungry, flagging, two hours from dinner
occasions.competes_with: biscuits from the office jar, a chocolate bar, samosa/vada from the canteen, chai, a banana, or skipping it entirely
occasions.decided_by: speed, taste, what is within arm's reach, mild guilt
occasions.channel: office pantry, vending machine, the desk drawer stocked on Blinkit

occasions.moment: 11pm, scrolling in bed, wants something sweet
occasions.competes_with: chocolate, ice cream, leftover mithai, biscuits, nothing
occasions.decided_by: craving, what is in the fridge, 10-minute delivery
occasions.channel: Blinkit / Zepto / Instamart, the kitchen cupboard

occasions.moment: straight after the gym, 45 minutes before a proper meal
occasions.competes_with: a whey shake, eggs, a banana, dal-chawal at home, nothing
occasions.decided_by: protein per serving, habit, what the trainer said
occasions.channel: gym counter, HealthKart, Amazon, the gym bag

occasions.moment: leaving the house late, will not sit down to eat
occasions.competes_with: toast, poha, cereal, a bought sandwich, coffee alone, skipping
occasions.decided_by: one hand, no crumbs, keeps until 11am
occasions.channel: kitchen counter, the metro station kiosk, monthly grocery order

occasions.moment: a weekend or a bad day — wants a treat but not to feel bad about it
occasions.competes_with: dark chocolate, a 'healthy' dessert, regular chocolate anyway, fruit
occasions.decided_by: permission — whether it reads as a treat or as a compromise
occasions.channel: quick commerce, the supermarket aisle, a cafe

occasions.moment: airport, long drive, or a two-hour commute with no real meal in sight
occasions.competes_with: airport sandwich, chips, nuts, a Snickers at the counter, nothing
occasions.decided_by: portability, shelf life, what the counter is selling
occasions.channel: airport store, highway stop, petrol pump, packed from home

occasions.moment: a standing daily habit someone has decided to keep
occasions.competes_with: a powder, gummies, a multivitamin, real food, nothing
occasions.decided_by: routine, whether it is working, cost per day
occasions.channel: Amazon subscribe, HealthKart, the pharmacy, D2C

occasions.moment: the monthly or weekly shop — buying for other people as well as themselves
occasions.competes_with: biscuit packs, namkeen, cereal, whatever the kids will eat
occasions.decided_by: price per unit, family acceptance, keeps in the cupboard

everyday_alternatives: Cadbury Dairy Milk — ₹10 to ₹100 depending on size; the default sweet thing
Snickers — ~₹40 for 50g; the 'it's basically food' bar at the counter
Britannia Good Day, Marie Gold, 50-50, Bourbon — ₹10-₹40 biscuit packs
Parle-G — ₹5-₹10; the floor of the category
Sunfeast Dark Fantasy — ~₹30; the indulgent biscuit
Lay's / Kurkure / Bingo — ₹20 chips and namkeen
Haldiram's namkeen — ₹20-₹50 packs, and the household tin
Amul / Kwality Walls ice cream — ₹40-₹80 for the late-night version
canteen samosa, vada pav, or chai — ₹10-₹25, hot and immediate
a banana or an apple from the fruit cart — ₹10-₹20
leftover mithai in the fridge after any festival
nothing at all — waiting it out until the next meal

raw.label: loyalist_four_o_clock_chai
raw.l1_context: Never came to it. The afternoon gap has been filled by the same tea and the same two biscuits for twenty years, and nothing has asked to replace it.
raw.l2_category: Buys the tea packet monthly at the kirana and a small biscuit pack every few days; ₹10-₹40 spends, on the shop tab.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows which biscuit softens in tea and which does not. Does NOT know what a protein bar is or costs. Does NOT know that shops sell anything called a supplement outside a pharmacy.
raw.l4_stance: Wants the afternoon tea and something to dip. Rejects anything eaten dry from a wrapper — says it is not food, it is timepass.
raw.l5_behavior: Sent the boy from the shop for a Marie Gold pack last week because the tin was empty before the afternoon tea.

raw.label: switcher_shrinking_biscuit_pack
raw.l1_context: Noticed the same pack held fewer biscuits than it used to, and started moving between brands and to the loose stuff from the bakery instead.
raw.l2_category: Buys whatever is heaviest for the coin at the kirana; changes brand every couple of months; keeps a steel tin, never a wrapper on the table.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows the count in a pack has dropped and which shop sells loose biscuits by weight. Does NOT know what 'high protein' on a wrapper means. Does NOT know these bars are sold in boxes online.
raw.l4_stance: Wants weight for the money and no air in the packet. Rejects branded snacks that shrink quietly — will walk to the bakery instead.
raw.l5_behavior: Stopped buying the Good Day pack after counting what came out and now buys loose ₹20 nankhatai from the bakery near the bus stand.

raw.label: upgrader_report_number_afternoon
raw.l1_context: A blood report last year put sugar at the edge, and the doctor said cut the evening biscuits. Started hunting for something to hold the 4pm gap instead.
raw.l2_category: Orders on a ten-minute app twice a month, ₹100-₹400 packs; buys roasted chana and one better-for-you thing, keeps it in her own steel dabba.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows the malt tin has sugar high in the list because her daughter showed her. Does NOT know whether the protein number on a bar is tested or true. Does NOT know one whey brand from another.
raw.l4_stance: Wants something filling with less sugar that she can eat at 4pm without a plate. Rejects anything the family will finish in one day.
raw.l5_behavior: Ordered a single RiteBite Max Protein bar on Blinkit after her daughter mentioned it; ate half, kept the rest for the next afternoon.

raw.label: aspirant_daughter_sends_reels
raw.l1_context: Her daughter in the city keeps forwarding reels about women her age needing protein and calcium. She has started thinking about it, not buying it.
raw.l2_category: Has never bought anything from this half of the shelf; buys the household biscuits and namkeen; watches, saves, does not order.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows the word protein and that women her age are told they lack it. Does NOT know where these bars are sold in her town. Does NOT know what a box of eight costs or that singles exist.
raw.l4_stance: Wants to try one thing that helps her knees and the afternoon tiredness. Rejects buying a whole box on trust — will not spend that on herself unseen.
raw.l5_behavior: Asked her daughter on a call whether the bar in the reel is available in the medical shop near the temple; has not ordered it.

raw.label: skeptic_ghee_dal_afternoon
raw.l1_context: Saw a nephew's expensive tub sit unopened in a cupboard for a year, and heard on the news that many of these protein packs test false.
raw.l2_category: Buys nothing from this half. Afternoon is leftover rotis with jaggery, or nothing at all until dinner.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows a lot of these labels were found wrong in testing. Does NOT know what these bars taste like, having never eaten one. Does NOT know the difference between a protein bar and a malt drink.
raw.l4_stance: Wants food cooked at home and no money going on wrappers. Rejects 'guilt-free' and 'high protein' outright — reads them as a shop's talk to frighten women.
raw.l5_behavior: Told her neighbour to keep her ₹80 and eat two chapatis with ghee instead of the bar someone had recommended for tiredness.
